newsitem.title: ITALY: Nude protest at summit over soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Nude protest at summit over soybeans.

text.p: A group of demonstrators stripped naked on Wednesday at a news conference with U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman at the World Food Summit.

The demonstrators, several of them women, appeared to be protesting against the sale of genetically modified U.S. soybeans. One woman's body was painted with the slogan "The Naked Truth". They had a banner saying "Ban the Gene Bean".
It was not clear how the protesters got into the venue, at the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) headquarters in Rome.
Police at the summit, focus of Italy's biggest single peacetime security operation, appeared caught off guard. They later escorted the demonstrators from the news conference.
An Italian protester, who identified herself as Olivia, said: "We're not part of any organisation. We are protesting against the genetic engineering of soybeans."

Protests by European environmentalists have gathered pace this week against the start of sales of the beans, which have been genetically changed to withstand treatment with Roundup, a weedkiller. They say the beans, developed by U.S. firm Monsanto Co, are a risky experiment with nature and could harm health.
